Available capacity equals configured slot capacity minus existing non-cancelled bookings and active holds; a hold expires after 15 minutes.
Scenario 3: Voucher, Staff Preference & Booking Creation
Optional discounts and staff preferences are validated before a transactional booking is created from the active slot hold.
Customer provides an optional promotion or voucher code.
Backend checks eligibility, validity and discount result.
Load staff candidates available for the selected time.
Customer selects preferred staff or automatic assignment.
Frontend submits vehicle, offering, slot and payment choice.
Backend validates hold, capacity, voucher and ownership.
Persist booking/payment, consume voucher and delete hold.
Response includes booking status and payment information.
Booking creation is server-authoritative: the active hold is removed only after the booking transaction succeeds, preventing duplicate capacity usage.
Online payment is verified by the backend before the booking becomes confirmed and eligible for wash operations.
Choose supported payment option during booking creation.

Customer pays using the generated bank-transfer content.

Dashed connection: SePay webhook or VNPay IPN/query callback is verified by Spring Boot before confirmation
The frontend never confirms an online payment by itself; only a verified SePay webhook or VNPay IPN/query result can mark the booking CONFIRMED.
Operational users turn a confirmed booking into a wash session and advance it through controlled lifecycle transitions.
Staff or manager views operational booking data.
Only confirmed bookings can start a wash session.
Use assignment, availability and workload information.
Create session linked to booking and assigned staff.
Operational queue accepts the prepared wash session.
Staff confirms the vehicle has arrived for service.
Session and booking move to active execution.
Save lifecycle state and publish realtime update.
Lifecycle transitions are validated by the backend: PENDING -> QUEUED -> CHECKED_IN -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED, with CANCELLED as a terminal alternative.
Scenario 6: Wash Progress & Realtime Customer Tracking
The customer follows the active wash session while staff actions update persisted state and notify subscribed dashboards.
Customer opens the active booking or tracking page.
Load active tracking or a selected session by ID.
Resolve booking, status, staff and timestamps.
PostgreSQL remains the authoritative session state.

Backend emits booking or wash-session update.
React Query caches are invalidated and reloaded.
Customer sees latest status, staff and timing data.
Dashed connection: STOMP /topic/bookings event causes subscribed clients to invalidate and reload React Query data
WebSocket improves freshness but does not replace persisted state; reconnecting clients reload data and polling remains the fallback mechanism.
Completing the wash finalizes operational and payment state, awards points, updates tier progress, and unlocks a booking review.

Reviews are accepted only for COMPLETED bookings, are limited to one per booking, and can store before/after image URLs in AWS S3.
